Policymaker session for issue #42 on branch `task/42`. Trigger: the first iteration of the loop. Iteration 0000 failed `stalled` with 0 tasks after 180303 s. `no_progress` is 1 and there are no pending suggestions.

## Changed
- `policy/params.yml` `routing.tasks`:
  - The planning roles (orchestrator, policymaker, researcher, benchmark, evaluator) now fall back to `codex/gpt-6.1-sol` instead of `gpt-6-astra`.
  - Why: orchestrator session #27 spent 2.86M astra input tokens for 9.6k output and produced no accepted result. `docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` rates sol about 5x cheaper for 1–2 index points.
- `policy/params.yml` review routes: `evaluator-verifier`, `review` and `reviewer` now start on `codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, then `claude-sonnet-5-5`, then `copilot/gpt-5.6-luna`.
  - Why: model-selection.md says luna is a first-pass filter, not a sole reviewer. Starting review on another model family also keeps it independent of the Claude-first implementation and evaluator routes.
  - `audit` keeps luna first.
- `execution/roles/orchestrator/SKILL.md`: the orchestrator now reads the roles it may order from `.session/capabilities.json` instead of `execution/profiles.yml` / `policy/profiles.yml`.
  - Why: those files are not in the runner checkout. Session #27 got FileNotFoundError on them (`journal/0000.md`).

## Ordered
- `.session/orders.json` has one `audit` task, `audit-0001`, which runs beside the shaper. It writes `audit/0001.md` and measures:
  - tokens per provider/model for sessions #27 and #42;
  - where the 180303 s went;
  - the repeated runner stops on pending read-only actions (`journal/task-27-orchestrator.md`);
  - why the codex fallback used millions of input tokens for little output.
- It exports streams/actions for iterations 0–1, the record for iteration 0, and the reports of sessions 27 and 42.
- Why: before tuning `context` sizes, turn limits or routing further, I need numbers, not guesses.

## Not verified
The issue has no `## Verification` command. The only check run here: `policy/params.yml` parses with the intended routes, and `.session/orders.json` is valid JSON. Whether the engine accepts the routes and the order is shown only when the iteration opens.

## Discoveries
- The codex fallback's input-to-output ratio is about 300:1 in #27 and about 130:1 in #42 (`.session/reports/27.json`, `.session/loop-state.json`). This suggests the full context is re-sent on every request. The audit will confirm or rule this out.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
